summary: Configured sudo command logging on node1 to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log, kept out of general syslog, and verified it survives a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Set sudo syslog facility to local2 via /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-logging (Defaults syslog=local2, syslog_goodpri=notice), validated with visudo -c
Added /etc/rsyslog.d/49-sudo-commands.conf routing local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with a stop action so it is not also written to /var/log/messages
Pre-created the log file with root:root 0600 permissions
Verified baseline: sudo commands appeared in sudo-commands.log with user+timestamp, and 0 sudo entries leaked into /var/log/messages
Captured pre-restart boot_id and marker, issued systemctl reboot on node1 asynchronously so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (f54d7366... -> d9d11468...) and boot time updated, proving an actual restart

Post-restart: confirmed sudoers and rsyslog drop-ins still present, rsyslog active, ran a fresh sudo command, verified it logged to sudo-commands.log with user+timestamp and still excluded from /var/log/messages

evidence.requirement: Baseline capture before restart (config present, service healthy, boot identity)
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id f54d7366-0403-4b05-93bb-b5c0a1818892, confirmed rsyslog active, sudoers/rsyslog drop-ins present, and existing sudo-commands.log line count

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: tail of sudo-commands.log shows entries like 'Sep 29 07:51:55 node1 sudo[1285]: root : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/whoami' with timestamp and invoking user

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries are excluded from the general system log
evidence.summary: grep -c 'sudo:' /var/log/messages returned 0 both before and after reboot, confirming sudo entries never reach the general log
systemctl reboot issued in background with nohup/disown; exec call returned 'reboot command issued' successfully before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node actually restarted (connection loss + changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down mid-reboot); subsequent poll succeeded with boot_id d9d11468-51bd-4415-a287-3b8c8f880744, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: logging configuration persisted and functioning after reboot
evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers and rsyslog drop-ins still present, rsyslog active, boot time updated to 2026-09-29 07:52, a fresh sudo id command logged correctly to sudo-commands.log with user+timestamp, and 0 sudo entries in /var/log/messages
